options.text: Changes direction as it passes from one medium to another due to a change in speed
Spreads out after passing through a gap

questions.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of a wave when it passes from one medium to another, caused by a change in wave speed.

questions.stem: When light enters a denser medium (e.g. air to glass), it bends:
questions.explanation: When light enters a denser medium, it slows down and bends toward the normal. The angle of refraction is less than the angle of incidence.

questions.stem: When a wave is refracted, which property does NOT change?
questions.explanation: The frequency of a wave is set by the source and does not change during refraction. The speed and wavelength both change, and the direction changes if the wave enters at an angle.

questions.stem: When light passes from glass back into air, it bends:
questions.explanation: When light enters a less dense medium (glass to air), it speeds up and bends away from the normal. The angle of refraction is greater than the angle of incidence.

options.text: Light in a denser medium hits the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle
Light hits a surface at exactly 0 degrees
Light is completely absorbed by the material

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light travelling in a denser medium hits the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing all light to be reflected back.

questions.stem: If light enters a glass block along the normal (at 0 degrees to the normal), it will:
questions.explanation: If light enters along the normal (angle of incidence = 0 degrees), it still slows down but does not change direction. Bending only occurs when light enters at an angle.

questions.stem: Why does a swimming pool appear shallower than it actually is?

options.text: Because light refracts (bends) as it passes from water to air, changing the apparent position of the bottom

questions.explanation: Light from the pool bottom refracts (bends away from the normal) as it passes from water into air, making the bottom appear closer to the surface than it really is.
